summary: The Variant sync on 2 July 2026 reviewed active work and new shredding inference benchmarks. Four strategies were compared with an unshredded baseline on 100k-row workloads, and the 'Wilson' strategy, which adds a statistical confidence interval before shredding, is the leading candidate. The current read benchmarks were judged misleading because they measure Spark's full-object re-serialization, so they will be reworked to simulate direct column extraction. Variant filter pushdown is blocked until Iceberg supports Spark 4.3; Qiegang Long will look into a backport to Spark 4.2. Several PRs await review.

topics.title: Active work and pending reviews
topics.summary: Several PRs are waiting for review: Qiegang Long's reader improvements, vectorized reader correctness fixes for decimal types and upper bounds, hardening limits to align with Parquet, and Steve's benchmark PR. For other languages, the Go reader is merged and the writer is in progress, Rust is in progress and likely for the 0.10 release, and Python is blocked by Arrow C++ progress. In Arrow C++, Jared Yu is refactoring the decoding/encoding PRs to be more idiomatic C++ in response to review feedback.

topics.title: Spark integration and filter pushdown
topics.summary: The expression builder has merged into DSv2. Variant filter pushdown is blocked by an API change in Spark 4.3, which introduces a dedicated expression API replacing the less efficient UDF-based approach. This delays filter pushdown until Iceberg adds Spark 4.3 support. Qiegang Long will investigate backporting the API change to Spark 4.2.
open_questions: Can the Spark 4.3 variant expression API change be backported to Spark 4.2?

topics.title: Shredding inference benchmarks
topics.summary: The goal was the inference strategy that best balances file size and write speed. Four strategies were compared with an unshredded baseline on 100k-row workloads on a local machine: B1 Majority (current; shreds if a primitive type appears in more than 10% of a 100-row sample), V2 Uniform (only if the type is 100% uniform in the sample), V2 Wilson (adds a confidence interval, for example 90%, to the B1 check), and B20 Uniform (uniform with a 20-row sample). Wilson is the leading candidate: it avoids the file-size waste of B1 Majority on polymorphic data, with write times comparable to B1 and read times slightly better in some cases. Future runs will use larger real-world datasets such as Netflix data and ClickBench.

topics.title: Read benchmark rework
topics.summary: The current read benchmarks were called misleading because they measure Spark's expensive full-object re-serialization rather than core reader performance. New benchmarks will simulate direct column extraction, which is the key performance goal. Read performance will be re-evaluated after the reader improvements merge.
